subject: [PATCH 05/12] mm/collapse: state what a collapse may do in the policy

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Baolin Wang noted that the check for mTHP collapse is stricter than described and suggested renaming the field 'allow_mthp_collapse' to clarify its purpose, allowing the original comments in collapse_max_ptes_xxx() functions to remain clear.

Reviewer Baolin Wang requested simplification of comments in the code, specifically suggesting that the explanation for 'install_pmd' be made easier to understand.
reviews.raw_body:
This is a bit confusing to me. Actually, the check for mTHP collapse is 
stricter.

How about naming it 'allow_mthp_collapse'? That way we can keep the most 
original comments for the collapse_max_ptes_xxx() functions, which is 
clearer to me.

If others have a better name, please ignore my comment.

---

Can you simplify theses comments? I think the 'install_pmd' is easy to 
expalain. :)

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed Zi Yan's concern that the collapse_policy struct should be a constant pointer to a caller-owned object, explaining that khugepaged fills it once per pass from sysfs knobs and madvise needs to initialize it after cc is allocated. The author prefers to keep it embedded rather than tracking its lifetime.
reviews.raw_body:
Not as a member: khugepaged fills it once per pass from the sysfs knobs,
so there is no constant object to point at. And madvise has to
initialize it somehow after cc is allocated.

It could become a const pointer to a struct the caller owns, but that
adds a lifetime to track for a struct that is written in one place and
read everywhere else.  I would rather keep it embedded.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed reviewer Baolin Wang's concern about the strict_sub_pmd flag, explaining that it is already decided elsewhere in the code and should not be duplicated as a separate flag. The author agreed to keep the existing implementation.
reviews.raw_body:
I would rather keep strict_sub_pmd.

Which orders a caller asks for is already decided elsewhere:
collapse_possible_orders() hands khugepaged every anonymous order and
MADV_COLLAPSE the PMD order only, from tva_type.

A flag called allow_mthp_collapse next to that would read as
a second place deciding the same thing, and flipping it would not change
which orders get collapsed.  What it does change is how a sub-PMD window
is judged once one is asked for, and it is read at exactly the three
places that judge one.

I will do:

      /* Take no swapped-out or shared PTE into a sub-PMD collapse */
      bool strict_sub_pmd;

2026-09-07.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new struct collapse_policy that allows the caller to specify what a collapse is allowed to do, such as setting limits on PTEs and determining whether to hold sub-PMD windows to stricter rules. The policy is filled in by khugepaged once per scan pass and by MADV_COLLAPSE once per call. This change simplifies the code by removing the need for tests scattered throughout the collapse path to determine what a collapse can do, instead allowing them to simply read from the policy struct.

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: Agreed with Kiryl's proposal and thanked him for the suggestion.
reviews.raw_body:
On 9/7/26 6:56 PM, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> On Mon, Sep 07, 2026 at 05:05:19PM +0800, Baolin Wang wrote:
>>> +/* What a collapse is allowed to do, decided by the caller that asks for it */
>>> +struct collapse_policy {
>>> +	/* Limits, stated per PMD; HPAGE_PMD_NR means "no limit" */
>>> +	unsigned int max_ptes_none;
>>> +	unsigned int max_ptes_swap;
>>> +	unsigned int max_ptes_shared;
>>> +
>>> +	/*
>>> +	 * Hold a sub-PMD window to a stricter rule than a PMD: no swapped-out
>>> +	 * and no shared PTEs at all, and max_ptes_none as
>>> +	 * collapse_max_ptes_none() scales it.
>>> +	 */
>>> +	bool strict_sub_pmd;
>>
>> This is a bit confusing to me. Actually, the check for mTHP collapse is
>> stricter.
>>
>> How about naming it 'allow_mthp_collapse'? That way we can keep the most
>> original comments for the collapse_max_ptes_xxx() functions, which is
>> clearer to me.
>>
>> If others have a better name, please ignore my comment.
> 
> I would rather keep strict_sub_pmd.
> 
> Which orders a caller asks for is already decided elsewhere:
> collapse_possible_orders() hands khugepaged every anonymous order and
> MADV_COLLAPSE the PMD order only, from tva_type.
> 
> A flag called allow_mthp_collapse next to that would read as
> a second place deciding the same thing, and flipping it would not change
> which orders get collapsed.  What it does change is how a sub-PMD window
> is judged once one is asked for, and it is read at exactly the three
> places that judge one.
> 
> I will do:
> 
>        /* Take no swapped-out or shared PTE into a sub-PMD collapse */
>        bool strict_sub_pmd;

OK. Fair enough. Thanks.

2026-09-08.patch_summary: The patch introduces a new flag called strict_sub_pmd to control sub-PMD window judgment in collapse.
